split_report.unit: generation batch (one LLM generation call); classes are NOT held out

protocol.class_text: label. description. Path: root > ... > label. Also called synonyms. (olaya.embedding_router.class_context_text)
protocol.state_text: the raw observation text (string state), for every router including the lexical one
protocol.candidate_policy: engine rows marked [routed] score every routed concept (OLaya(candidate_policy='routed')); unmarked rows score the routed leaves only (default, shared with the Rust / Node runtimes)
protocol.hybrid_union: interleave lexical and embedding top lists
protocol.scorer: cosine similarity of the state to the class text, temperature fitted on the calibration split concept tasks (gold + 5 hard negatives)
protocol.selection: every 'best' / 'default' choice below is made on the validation split; test is evaluated once per configuration

task.temperature_fit: grid search of the masked NLL on the calibration tasks, base * 10^[-2, 2]

limitations: Labels are LLM-distilled (generated for a class by one model, kept only when a second model agreed) and filtered; they are not human labels.
The split holds out generation batches (register x seed), not classes; the fine-tuned encoder has seen almost every test class in training (see corpus.split_report).
Zero-shot encoders never saw the corpus; their temperature is the only fitted parameter (calibration split).
The concept-task metrics have the gold candidate present (5 hard negatives); the full-ontology and engine-path numbers are the deployment comparison.
The state passed to every router is the raw observation text; the decision head reports used a JSON state wrapper for the engine path.
